claims.statement: For iid X,X' with cap-one density f and the unnormalized sum/difference kernel Psi_f(u,s), integral integral |Psi_f(u,s)|^p ds du <= pi for every p>=2; at p=2 equality is pi||f||_2^4. Consequently integral integral |a(u)||Psi_f(u,t a(u))|^p dt du <=pi for every measurable a.

For every physical coordinate j and p>=2, the exact quadratic decoupling obeys integral dt du |(Au)_j||Psi_j(u_j,t(Au)_j)|^p product_{k!=j}r_k(u_k)<=pi. Three-coordinate Holder yields the weighted product estimate with W_S=(product |(Au)_j|)^(1/3)(product r_j)^(2/3).

For f=1_[0,1], lambda!=0 and any p>0, integral_{|u|<1/2} integral |Psi(u,t lambda u)|^p dt du diverges logarithmically, so the exact coefficient Jacobian weight cannot be dropped by absolute-value/Fubini pullback. This is not a QFORM counterexample.

partner_application.inequality: For Q_epsilon=X0^2+Z^T S_epsilon Z with 0<=epsilon<=1/4 and S_epsilon=[[1,1,1,epsilon],[1,1,-1,-epsilon],[1,-1,1,0],[epsilon,-epsilon,0,0]], the partner theorem gives ||p_Qepsilon||_infinity<240 uniformly.

first_unpaid_description: Under s_3(A)>=1, combine the weighted three-coordinate sum/difference estimate with a product-preserving grouped/projected-crossing receiver on the region where W_S is small, without dividing by conditional-density factors and without requiring a uniformly good single minor.
